workflows.purpose: Prepare checked staging documentation imports from the two allowlisted stable source repositories without automating production promotion.
steps: Resolve an exact main source revision with a successful same-repository export run, then re-export its committed documentation and licence with read-only permissions.
Validate a same-run bounded snapshot against immutable source Git objects and complete provenance before an isolated writer replaces only the owned section on its generated staging PR.
Use a separate Actions-writing job to verify the actual generated PR, dispatch the existing documentation and branch-policy checks on its exact head, and bind the returned run identities.
outputs: A seven-day docs-import-<source>-<run-id>-<run-attempt> artifact and an opened, updated or pending section-only staging PR when content changes; valid unchanged content creates no PR.
Verified requested run URLs for the two existing required checks; the workflow never merges a PR or promotes production.

workflows.purpose: Validate normal pull-request branch relationships and narrowly verified generated-PR dispatches without granting the policy job token permissions.
steps: For ordinary PR events, read GitHub event metadata without checkout and require staging or main as the base; only same-repository staging may target main.
For generated dispatches, refuse foreign repository, branch, head or helper identities before anonymously fetching the central validator at the running workflow commit.
Validate actual API PR metadata, current head/base and the complete generated-only change proof for docs imports or the organisation map before reporting the same required check.
outputs: The stable Validate branch policy job result, failing on malformed events, unsupported generated identities, source proof failures or ref movement.

workflows.purpose: Publish separate staging prereleases and stable releases from an exact same-repository staging promotion, without changing the legacy owner-approved release path.
steps: Validate the public push identity, immutable package and changelog, active branch rules and pre-existing channel environment; stable requires the exact merged staging pull request and both merge parents.
Prepare only supported root manifest and lock versions, then run consumer checks, build and script-free packing with read-only permissions.
Recheck authority and committed source, bind same-run artifacts to repository, commit, channel, version and attempt, and validate plain files and strict package archives before attestation.
Atomically reserve a new tag, publish npm with an explicit registry and staging or latest tag from an isolated environment, create the prerelease or stable release page, and verify the tag again.
outputs: Derived version and channel, with released=true only after successful publication and exact tag verification; source version 0.0.0 skips publication.
Immutable version tags, release pages and optional attested assets and GitHub Packages versions; no caller adoption or environment changes.

Refusal on unavailable evidence, invalid promotion, incompatible protections, unsupported package/lock data, artifact mismatch or reused version. Hidden ruleset bypasses and human intent require separate settings and process controls.

workflows.purpose: Prepare a generated-only organisation-map staging pull request and request its existing required checks without merging or promoting production.
steps: Run only for unset-sh/.github staging pushes, schedules or manual calls; regenerate and check the exact source with read-only permissions.
Publish only MAP.md and the generated profile block through an isolated bot-owned staging PR, verifying exact source/head trees and preserving authored profile text.

Pass only the PR number, head and base to a separate Actions-write job that revalidates the real PR and dispatches the fixed organisation-map, documentation-check and branch-policy workflows at that exact head.
outputs: An open generated staging PR when output changes, plus links to its three requested check runs. Successful dispatch does not prove those checks passed. No automatic merge or main promotion occurs.

workflows.purpose: Refresh the published documentation maps hourly while staging remains the default branch and main remains the production source.
steps: Run at minute 23 each hour or by manual dispatch on staging, with serial timer runs.
Call the reviewed tooling dispatcher with contents-read and Actions-write permissions to request only the existing main site workflow.
outputs: A main site workflow run requested by the central dispatcher. The timer neither promotes staging content nor establishes that deployment succeeded.

workflows.purpose: Refresh supported upstream content and registered maps, build the organisation documentation site and publish it on GitHub Pages.
steps: On main pushes or manual main runs, call the shared map workflow to refresh every registered map and return one validated snapshot; the separate default-branch timer requests hourly runs.
After the map refresh succeeds, resolve the latest compatible published brand release, install the pinned tooling without lifecycle scripts and download this run's validated map snapshot.
Run the source and publication guards, build the publication site with Hugo and check its rendered pages, navigation and workflow map.
Upload the public directory as a Pages artifact, then deploy it through the github-pages environment; only the deployment job receives Pages publication permissions.
outputs: A validated map artifact for this run and a checked Pages artifact, followed by the published documentation site when deployment succeeds.
Brand, organisation-map and workflow-map updates used by this build; the workflow does not commit these updates back to the repository.

workflows.purpose: Check and package tooling’s own maintained documentation using the shared workflows it provides.
steps: Run the shared Node checks under the distinct validate-docs / Check context on pull requests, main pushes and manual runs.
After validation succeeds, export the committed tooling docs and licence with source revision and file hashes.
Upload the provenance-bearing section for downstream import; this workflow does not write the docs repository or deploy the site.
outputs: A docs-<commit> artifact retained for 14 days; publication is a separate step.

workflows.purpose: Keep the docs site’s approved main build refreshing every registered map when staging is the default branch.
steps: Accept only scheduled or manual calls from unset-sh/docs on staging, and run the central helper at the exact reusable-workflow commit.
Use the docs job token to request only site.yml on main through the fixed GitHub workflow-dispatch endpoint; no consumer code runs and no repository content is written.
Validate the returned run identity and print its URL so collection, build and deployment can be verified separately.
outputs: A requested main site run. A successful dispatch is not proof that the map refresh or site deployment succeeded.

workflows.purpose: Prepare the organisation’s maintained documentation for the central docs site after regenerating and checking the organisation map.
steps: Through the shared CI workflow, regenerate MAP.md and the profile map block from repos.json, then run the organisation’s tests and check the generated result.
After validation succeeds, export the committed docs/site pages and licence into the github section with source revision and file hashes.
Upload the isolated export for a later publishing step; regenerated map views are not committed or included as documentation sources by this workflow.
outputs: A docs-<commit> artifact retained for 14 days, containing the github documentation section and provenance; this workflow does not publish to the docs repository.

workflows.purpose: Prepare the organisation’s maintained documentation for the central docs site after the organisation checks pass.
steps: Run the organisation’s tests and verify that its generated map matches repos.json through the shared CI workflow.
Export the committed docs/site pages and licence into the github section with source revision and file hashes.
Upload the isolated export for a later publishing step; this workflow does not write to the docs repository.
outputs: A docs-<commit> artifact retained for 14 days, containing the github documentation section and provenance.

workflows.purpose: Keep the committed organisation map and profile map block current after their source changes, using the reviewed shared publisher.
steps: Run for relevant main-branch changes, on the hourly schedule and on demand; serialize publication runs without cancelling an active run.
Call the shared organisation-map publisher at a full reviewed commit, which regenerates and checks the registered outputs with read-only permissions.
Use its separate publisher to validate the same-run snapshot and preserve authored profile text, then prepare a generated-only pull request and request its exact-head squash merge.
Respect GitHub merge restrictions and stop on observed main movement; a successful current-main run recovers a view made stale by a concurrent base change.
outputs: The shared publisher’s seven-day org-map-<run-id>-<run-attempt> artifact.
Updated MAP.md and the generated profile/README.md block when output changed and GitHub permits the merge, or a prepared PR when the merge is refused; unchanged output creates no PR.

workflows.purpose: Validate the organisation map regenerated from its curated source and report differences between that source and public GitHub repositories.
steps: On pull requests and main changes, regenerate the map and profile from repos.json, then run tests and check the generated result without committing it.
On daily scheduled or manual runs, compare public repository names, descriptions, archive status and licences with the curated map; private entries are skipped.
Create or update one org-map-drift issue when differences appear, and close it when the comparison matches.
Leave ownership descriptions and source metadata to a reviewed source change; the drift job does not rewrite repos.json, while the separate publisher updates derived Markdown views.
outputs: Validation results for the regenerated organisation map.
An automatically maintained drift issue when public repository metadata differs.

workflows.purpose: Keep the curated organisation map consistent with its source and report differences between the map and public GitHub repositories.
steps: On pull requests and main changes, run tests and check that the generated map and profile match repos.json.
On scheduled or manual runs, compare public repository names, descriptions, archive status and licences with the curated map; private entries are skipped.
Create or update one org-map-drift issue when differences appear, and close it when the comparison matches.
Leave ownership descriptions and map edits for a reviewed source change; the drift job does not rewrite repos.json.
outputs: Validation results for the generated organisation map.
An automatically maintained drift issue when public repository metadata differs.

workflows.purpose: Check that the shared agent rules, skills and synchronisation tools can be distributed as a consistent bundle.
steps: Run the repository’s checks against the kit and its synchronisation behaviour.
Collect the shipped rules, skills, agents and sync.mjs into a deterministically ordered bundle.
Record the source commit, kit version and each shipped file’s SHA-256 in the bundle.
outputs: A locally built dist/agent-kit.json and its checksum in the job log; CI does not upload or publish the bundle.

workflows.purpose: Publish a tagged version of the agent kit so repositories can adopt a specific, verifiable bundle.
steps: Require the tag to match package.json and its commit to be reachable from main.
Run the kit checks, build agent-kit.json, copy sync.mjs and extract the version’s release notes.
Pass those files through the release artifact to the publishing job, which uses the release environment.
Verify the artifact’s file set, attest the bundle and synchronisation script, and create the GitHub release from the existing tag.
outputs: A GitHub release containing agent-kit.json and sync.mjs, with release notes.
Attestations for the two downloadable files and a seven-day intermediate release artifact.

workflows.purpose: Check the brand contract and package, then verify that the brand site builds at both a domain root and a repository subpath.
steps: Install the pinned dependencies and check that generated brand assets and syntax examples are current.
Run the brand and component-gallery tests.
Install the verified Hugo binary and build the site once at the root and once under /brand.
outputs: Validation results for the brand package and two local site builds; this workflow does not publish them.

workflows.purpose: Build and publish the brand guidelines and component gallery on GitHub Pages.
steps: Check out main, install the pinned dependencies and verified Hugo version, and run the brand checks.
Build the site using the base path and URL supplied by GitHub Pages.
Upload site/public as a Pages artifact.
Deploy that artifact in a separate job using the github-pages environment.
outputs: The generated brand site as a Pages artifact and, after deployment succeeds, its published Pages URL.

workflows.purpose: Publish a checked, tagged brand package to GitHub Packages.
steps: Require the tag to match package.json and the tagged commit to be reachable from main.
Install dependencies, run the brand checks and pack the package once without package lifecycle scripts.
Record its SHA-256 and retain the package artifact for the publishing job.
In the release environment, require exactly one package archive, attest it and publish that same archive to GitHub Packages.
outputs: The @unset-sh/brand package and its artifact attestation.
A seven-day package artifact and checksum summary; this workflow does not create a GitHub release page.

workflows.purpose: Check documentation sources, publication safeguards and rendered pages before changes reach the documentation site.
steps: Install the pinned tooling without lifecycle scripts and run the Node and Python checks, workflow guards and organisation-map integrity check.
For pull requests, check whether the changes have the required documentation impact.
Lint the workflow files with the pinned actionlint image.
Build the real documentation and a separate fixture preview, checking generated HTML, assets, links and navigation.
outputs: Validation results and local builds of the real site and documentation fixtures; CI does not deploy them.

workflows.purpose: Refresh supported upstream content and registered maps, build the organisation documentation site and publish it on GitHub Pages.
steps: On main-branch pushes, manual runs and the hourly schedule, call the pinned shared refresh workflow to generate and validate the registered organisation and workflow maps.
After the map refresh succeeds, resolve the latest compatible published brand release, install the pinned tooling without lifecycle scripts and download this run's validated map snapshot.
Run the source and publication guards, build the publication site with Hugo and check its rendered pages, navigation and workflow map.
Upload the public directory as a Pages artifact, then deploy it through the github-pages environment; only the deployment job receives Pages publication permissions.
outputs: A validated map artifact for this run and a checked Pages artifact, followed by the published documentation site when deployment succeeds.
Brand, organisation-map and workflow-map updates used by this build; the workflow does not commit these updates back to the repository.

workflows.purpose: Refresh supported upstream content, build the organisation documentation site and publish it on GitHub Pages.
steps: Resolve the latest compatible published brand release and refresh the organisation map from a fixed source revision.
Install the pinned tooling and run the source and publication guards.
Build the publication site with Hugo and verify the rendered output and required section landing pages.
Upload the public directory as a Pages artifact, then deploy it through the github-pages environment.
outputs: A checked Pages artifact and, after deployment succeeds, the published documentation site.
Brand and organisation-map updates used by this build; the workflow does not commit these updates back to the repository.

workflows.purpose: Validate the AT Protocol lexicon schemas, examples and reference documentation together.
steps: Typecheck and lint the validation tooling, then run its tests.
Parse the schemas with the official AT Protocol libraries and build validators to resolve their references.
Validate authored examples and their coverage, and check generated reference documentation, local links and schema provenance hashes.
outputs: A check result reporting schema, example, documentation, link or provenance problems; no release or documentation export is published.

workflows.purpose: Check that eligible pull-request commits carry a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off.
steps: Read the pull request’s base and head commits from the full checkout history.
Exempt the owner’s and bot-authored pull requests, and ignore merge commits.
Report each remaining commit that lacks a correctly formed Signed-off-by line.
outputs: The DCO check result for the pull request.

workflows.purpose: Publish the checked profile-recipe documentation into its owned section of the central docs repository.
steps: Check out the current main branch, run typechecking, tests and recipe validation, and render the recipe catalogue.
Prepare an isolated profile-recipes export containing the guides, licences, example image and source hashes.
Require the configured publishing key and check out unset-sh/docs main.
Replace only profile-recipes/, verify that outgoing paths and files match the export, and commit and push changes without rewriting history; unchanged exports do not create a commit.
outputs: An updated profile-recipes section in unset-sh/docs when publishing credentials are configured and the push succeeds.
A source.json manifest identifying the recipe revision and exported file hashes.

workflows.purpose: Check that profile recipes satisfy their schemas and can produce the showcase and documentation export.
steps: Typecheck the tooling, run its tests and validate every recipe against the vendored upstream schemas.
Render the recipe showcase pages.
Prepare an isolated documentation export and check its source provenance without publishing it.
outputs: Recipe-validation results, locally rendered showcase pages and a temporary documentation export.

workflows.purpose: Check the image-rendering package and keep a visual gallery for reviewing its output.
steps: Install dependencies, then typecheck, lint, build the package and run its tests.
Attempt to draw the gallery even when an earlier check fails.
Upload any generated gallery output so reviewers can inspect the rendered images.
outputs: A gallery artifact retained for 14 days when gallery files are available.
Validation results and a local package build.

workflows.purpose: Publish a tagged image-rendering package after its release and dependency checks pass.
steps: Require the tag to match package.json, its commit to be reachable from main, and every runtime dependency to use an exact released version.
Install dependencies, typecheck, lint, build and test the package.
Pack once without lifecycle scripts, record its checksum and pass the archive to the publishing job.
In the release environment, require exactly one archive, attest it and publish that same archive to GitHub Packages.
outputs: The @unset-sh/presentation package and an artifact attestation when all release gates pass.
A seven-day package artifact and checksum summary; this workflow does not create a GitHub release page.

workflows.purpose: Validate that feature work enters staging and only same-repository staging promotes to main.
steps: Read the original pull-request event as JSON with no checkout, token permissions, repository code or API calls.
Reject missing or inconsistent metadata, non-PR events and bases other than staging or main.
Allow feature and fork PRs into staging; require a staging head from the same repository for main.
Report the branch-policy result without identifying a human, approving a PR or publishing anything.
outputs: The Validate branch policy job conclusion, for callers to require alongside their product checks.

workflows.purpose: Apply the shared PR branch policy to tooling itself.
steps: Run on all pull requests, including retargeting and ready-for-review events, without path or base filters.
Call the branch-policy implementation from the same commit with no token permissions.
outputs: The nested policy / Validate branch policy result; no merges, settings changes or releases.

workflows.purpose: Verify tooling’s implementation and the executable workflows generated from its organised workflow sources.
steps: Run for pull requests and pushes to staging or main.
Run the local reusable check workflow, which checks generated workflow files and runs tooling’s test suites.
Download the pinned actionlint release and verify its SHA-256.
Lint the executable workflow files, suppressing only the two documented job-context fields that the pinned linter does not recognise.
outputs: Check and workflow-lint results; this workflow does not release or publish tooling.

workflows.purpose: Provide a shared way to package committed public documentation with verifiable source information.
steps: Check out the calling repository at its event commit and the helper scripts at this reusable workflow’s own commit.
Read tooling documentation from docs/ and other consumers’ documentation from docs/site/, together with the root licence.
Validate the committed files and export them into the repository’s owned section with a source revision and SHA-256 manifest.
Upload the export as an artifact for later consumption; this workflow does not publish to the docs repository or a site.
outputs: A docs-<commit> artifact retained for 14 days, containing the documentation section, licence and source.json.

workflows.purpose: Check and package tooling’s own maintained documentation using the shared workflows it provides.
steps: Run tooling’s checks through the local reusable CI workflow.
After those checks pass, call the local documentation exporter.
Export the committed docs/ pages and licence into the tooling section with provenance.
outputs: A docs-<commit> artifact retained for 14 days; publication is a separate step.

workflows.purpose: Refresh every map registered by a calling repository and hand its build one complete validated JSON snapshot.
steps: Check out the caller at its event commit and the central helper at this reusable workflow’s own full commit.
Optionally install the caller’s locked dependencies with lifecycle scripts disabled, before passing a read-only token to generation.
Run each registered Node generator in order, then validate every declared output as a bounded regular JSON file under data/.
Stage and upload only the complete snapshot; a generator or validation failure prevents upload and stops a dependent build.
outputs: A maps-<run-id>-<run-attempt> artifact retained for seven days, preserving declared data/ paths.
The artifact-name output for a dependent same-run download; this workflow does not commit files or publish a site.

workflows.purpose: Regenerate the organisation’s Markdown map and publish validated changes through a generated-only pull request.
steps: Accept only unset-sh/.github main-branch push, scheduled or manual runs, and verify the reusable helper’s repository and full commit identity.
With read-only permissions, check out the exact source revision, regenerate and check the map, then stage only the two registered Markdown outputs in this run’s artifact.
In a separate job, check out only the pinned helper, download the same-run snapshot and give the write token only to the publisher.
Verify the source revision, fixed output paths and authored profile text, then create or reuse only a matching generated branch and bot-authored pull request with the bot sign-off.

Request a squash merge with the exact PR head, refusing observed main movement and respecting GitHub merge restrictions; a concurrent base change can leave a stale view until a successful current-main run.
outputs: An org-map-<run-id>-<run-attempt> artifact retained for seven days.
When output changes and GitHub permits the merge, updated MAP.md and the generated profile/README.md block; unchanged output creates no branch or PR.
A prepared pull request when GitHub refuses the merge; source declarations and authored profile text remain unchanged.

workflows.purpose: Provide a reusable Node-based check job that each calling repository configures with its own validation command.
steps: Check out the caller and select the Node version from its .nvmrc.
Optionally install dependencies with npm ci --ignore-scripts.
Run the caller’s check command, defaulting to npm run check.
If the caller specifies an output path, attempt to retain it even when the check fails.
outputs: The check result for the calling repository.
An optional check-output artifact retained for 14 days when a path is configured and files are available.

workflows.purpose: Verify tooling’s implementation and the executable workflows generated from its organised workflow sources.
steps: Run the local reusable check workflow, which checks generated workflow files and runs tooling’s test suites.
Download the pinned actionlint release and verify its SHA-256.
Lint the executable workflow files, suppressing only the two documented job-context fields that the pinned linter does not recognise.
outputs: Check and workflow-lint results; this workflow does not release or publish tooling.

workflows.purpose: Provide a shared release pipeline that builds once and publishes a new main-branch version through the owner’s release approval.
steps: Accept only a push to main, inspect package.json and existing tags, and skip version 0.0.0 or an unchanged version that is already released.
Before building, validate the release environment’s owner-only review and main-only branch policy, plus the package manifest and changelog.
Run the caller’s checks and optional build, collect configured release files and optionally pack an npm package, then show their checksums and notes for review.
After the release environment permits publication, recheck its protections and validate the downloaded artifacts without running the caller’s source code.
Attest the files, optionally publish the npm archive to GitHub Packages, create the tag and GitHub release, and verify that the tag names the intended commit.
outputs: A version tag and GitHub release with configured assets and release notes, plus attestations for attached files.
An optional GitHub Packages release and a seven-day intermediate release artifact.
The version and released workflow outputs for the caller.

workflows.purpose: Release tooling itself through its shared release pipeline, attaching the executable workflows so consumers can verify a chosen version.
steps: Start when package.json changes on main and call the local shared release workflow.
Run tooling’s checks and collect the executable files directly under .github/workflows as release assets.
Use the shared release environment checks and approval before attesting the workflow files and creating the version tag and release page.
At the reviewed source revision, package.json is still version 0.0.0, so the shared planner skips publication.
outputs: For a releasable version, a GitHub release containing attested workflow files; no npm package is requested.

workflows.purpose: Provide a shared way to package committed public documentation with verifiable source information.
steps: Check out the calling repository at its event commit and the helper scripts at this reusable workflow’s own commit.
Read the calling repository’s committed docs/site/ pages together with the root licence.
Validate the committed files and export them into the repository’s owned section with a source revision and SHA-256 manifest.
Upload the export as an artifact for later consumption; this workflow does not publish to the docs repository or a site.
outputs: A docs-<commit> artifact retained for 14 days, containing the documentation section, licence and source.json.

workflows.purpose: Provide a reusable Node-based check job that each calling repository configures with its own validation command.
steps: Check out the caller and select the Node version from its .nvmrc.
Optionally install dependencies with npm ci --ignore-scripts.
Run the caller’s check command, defaulting to npm run check.
If the caller specifies an output path, attempt to retain it even when the check fails.
outputs: The check result for the calling repository.
An optional check-output artifact retained for 14 days when a path is configured and files are available.

workflows.purpose: Validate current pull-request labels and readiness, validation and documentation declarations without executing pull-request code.
steps: Require a real pull-request event, bind its repository, number and head to current metadata fetched from the fixed GitHub API endpoint, and refuse changed or unavailable identities.
Require exactly one supported purpose label, one readiness choice, prerequisite and tested-combination fields, and authored validation and documentation sections.
Ignore comments and code examples, reject duplicate sections and placeholders, and run only the central helper at the exact reusable-workflow commit with read-only permissions.
outputs: A PR policy check result. This validates declarations, not their truth or sufficiency; it does not merge, release or grant a policy exception.

workflows.purpose: Apply the shared pull-request metadata check to tooling changes when their code, description or labels change.
steps: Run on opened, synchronized, reopened, edited, labeled, unlabeled and ready-for-review pull requests, without path filters.
Call tooling’s local reusable PR policy workflow with read-only contents and pull-request permissions, cancelling superseded runs for the same PR.
Use the repository’s purpose labels and PR template to make missing declarations actionable.
outputs: The policy / PR policy check on tooling pull requests. Ruleset enforcement and adoption in other repositories are separate rollout steps.

workflows.purpose: Check declared dependency and action pins, installed agent-kit integrity and forbidden working-artifact paths without executing consumer code.
steps: Verify the central workflow identity and check out the consumer and tooling helpers at their exact event and workflow commits.
Install checksum-verified zizmor 1.32.0, parse committed workflow and configured action definitions offline, and fail on parser or scanner errors.
Read the committed policy configuration and npm manifests, compare installed-kit bytes with their lock, inspect forbidden path prefixes, and apply only reasoned exact exceptions.
outputs: A Repository policy check result with bounded diagnostics. This does not establish semantic policy compliance, release authenticity, dependency age or licence correctness; other repositories must adopt it explicitly.

workflows.purpose: Apply the shared repository policy checks to tooling pull requests and staging or main pushes.
steps: Run on every pull request and pushes to staging or main without path filters.
Call the local reusable repository-policy workflow with read-only contents permission and tooling’s committed scope configuration.
outputs: The policy / Repository policy check for tooling. Ruleset enforcement remains a separate setting.
